answer: Real estate whose property taxes are delinquent is advertised and sold at public auction by the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes. The advertisement is titled "Delinquent Tax Sale".
quote: The property duly advertised must be sold, by the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes, at public auction at the courthouse or other convenient place within the county ... The property must be advertised for sale at public auction. The advertisement must be in a newspaper of general circulation within the county or municipality, if applicable, and must be entitled "Delinquent Tax Sale".
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: The sale is held on the advertised date. Real property must be advertised once a week for three consecutive weeks before the legal sales date.
quote: on the advertised date for legal tender payable in full ... The advertising must be published once a week before the legal sales date for three consecutive weeks for the sale of real property
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: The law requires a public auction at the courthouse or at another convenient place within the county, if that place is designated and advertised.
quote: at public auction at the courthouse or other convenient place within the county, if designated and advertised, on the advertised date
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
note: Chapter 51 sets no statewide bidder-registration rule that was found; registration is set by each county (see county rows).

source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
note: Chapter 51 requires the full bid on the day of the sale (see payment_deadline); no separate deposit rule was found.

answer: The officer conducting the sale submits a bid on behalf of the forfeited land commission equal to all unpaid property taxes, penalties, assessments and costs, including the taxes levied for the year in which the redemption period begins.
quote: shall submit a bid on behalf of the forfeited land commission equal to the amount of all unpaid property taxes, penalties, assessments including, but not limited to, assessments owed to a special taxing district established pursuant to Section 4-9-30, Chapter 19, Title 4, or an assessment district established pursuant to Chapter 15, Title 6, and costs including taxes levied for the year in which the redemption period begins.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: The successful bidder must pay the full amount of the bid on the day of the sale, in cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order. A bidder who fails to pay has the bid cancelled and is liable for up to five hundred dollars in damages.
quote: for legal tender payable in full by cash, cashier's check, certified check, or money order on the date of the sale. ... The successful bidder at the delinquent tax sale shall pay legal tender as provided in Section 12-51-50 to the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes in the full amount of the bid on the day of the sale. ... The defaulting bidder is liable for no more than five hundred dollars damages upon default
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: If the property is not redeemed, the purchaser pays the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus the documentary stamps and recording fees before the tax title is delivered for recording.
quote: The successful purchaser, or assignee, is responsible for the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus documentary stamps necessary to be affixed and recording fees.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: Yes. The defaulting taxpayer, a grantee from the owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within twelve months from the date of the sale. Interest on the bid runs from 3% (first three months) to 12% (last three months), and may not exceed the forfeited land commission's bid.
quote: The defaulting taxpayer, any grantee from the owner, or any mortgage or judgment creditor may within twelve months from the date of the delinquent tax sale redeem each item of real estate ... First three months three percent of the bid amount ... Last three months twelve percent of the bid amount However, in every redemption, the amount of interest due must not exceed the amount of the bid on the property submitted on behalf of the forfeited land commission pursuant to Section 12-51-55.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: If the property is not redeemed, the collector makes a tax title to the purchaser. The tax deed is prima facie evidence of good title, and after a further twelve months it is incontestable on procedural or other grounds.
quote: shall make a tax title to the purchaser or the purchaser's assignee. ... the tax deed issued is incontestable on procedural or other grounds. ... the deed of conveyance, whether executed to a private person, a corporation, or a forfeited land commission, is prima facie evidence of a good title in the holder
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: The opening bid is made on behalf of the county forfeited land commission. The commission sells the lands bid in for it, on terms it decides are in the best interest of the county.
quote: shall effect the sale of lands forfeited and bid in for the various forfeited land commissions of the State by the county auditors or the tax collectors of the several counties of the State in pursuance of Section 12-51-55. All lands deeded to the forfeited land commission of any county shall be held by it as assets of the county and sold to the best interest of the county.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
note: No statewide due-diligence statement was found; county pages carry their own (e.g. Horry, Oconee, Georgetown).

answer: These are lands bid in for the county forfeited land commission at the delinquent tax sale. The commission holds them as assets of the county and sells them, and it may also assign its bids before the tax deed is made.
quote: All lands deeded to the forfeited land commission of any county shall be held by it as assets of the county and sold to the best interest of the county. ... The forfeited land commission may assign its bids at any time before title deed being made pursuant to sale
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: For assignments of the commission's bids, the chairman may accept sealed bids for a set period; assignments not made then may be made first come, first served. The commission keeps a list of available properties at a location it chooses.
quote: The chairman or his designee may accept sealed bids for assignments of the forfeited land commission bids for a designated time period. Assignments not made during this time may then be assigned on a first come, first served basis. A list of available forfeited land commission properties is to be maintained at an assigned location as determined by the county forfeited land commission.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: An assignment of a commission bid may not be for less than the taxes, penalties and costs for which the property was sold.
quote: provided the consideration to be paid for such assignments shall not be less than the amount of taxes, penalties and costs for which the property was sold.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
note: Not stated in Chapter 59; set by each commission (see county rows).

source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
note: Not stated in Chapter 59; set by each commission (see county rows).

answer: Terms are set by the commission, but any terms may not run longer than ten years for full payment and must be secured by a first real estate mortgage on the property.
quote: but the terms of sale shall not in any case provide for a longer term than ten years for the full payment of the purchase price of such property and shall be secured by a first real estate mortgage upon the property sold.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: Deeds for land the commission sells are made by the forfeited land commission of the county holding title, or by a majority of its members.
quote: All deeds for lands sold under the authority of Section 12-59-40 shall be made by the forfeited land commission of the county holding title thereto or by a majority of the members thereof
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

answer: Online registration ends at 5:00 PM on Friday, November 20, 2026; in-person registration ends at 4:00 PM on Monday, November 30, 2026. There is no registration on the morning of the sale, and the fee is $25.00.

answer: All bids must be paid at the close of the sale, in cash or certified funds only. Personal or business checks and wire transfers are not accepted, and all sales are final.

answer: Fill out a separate FLC bid form for each property and submit it sealed, in person at the Horry County Assessor's Office in Conway or by certified mail marked "Confidential - FLC Bid", with the PIN on the outside. Do not include payment; the winning bidder is contacted with payment instructions.
quote: Bids should be submitted in person to the Horry County Assessor's Office in Conway, SC or sent via certified mail in an envelope marked "Confidential - FLC Bid". Please include the PIN number on the OUTSIDE of your sealed bid envelope. Please do NOT include payment with your bid. The winning bidder will be contacted and provided with payment instructions at that time. ... A separate offer form must be filled out for each property that you wish to make an offer on.
source_title: Horry County Forfeited Lands Commission - FLC Bid Form

answer: The minimum bid is the past and current taxes due, penalties and costs, plus 15% administrative fees set by the FLC. Offers above or below it may be made; the FLC may accept, decline or offer a compromise price.
quote: The FLC may accept a bid, decline a bid, or offer a compromise sale price. The minimum bid amount is determined by the amount of past and current taxes due, any penalties and costs, plus 15% additional administrative fees as defined by the FLC.
source_title: Horry County Forfeited Lands Commission - FLC Bid Form

answer: The FLC Bid Form, one per property, including either the Real Estate Property Identification Number or the Mobile Home Decal Number.

source_title: Horry County Forfeited Lands Commission - FLC Bid Form

answer: Do not send payment with the bid. The winning bidder is contacted and given payment instructions.
